reviews.one_line_contribution: A leave-one-type-out bank construction for ALFWorld (six banks, each missing one task type, every one of the 274 validation games read against the bank lacking its own type) used to re-measure agent-experience transfer with writer identity manipulated and a matched QLoRA arm, in support of three claims: measured retrieval gains are almost entirely same-type procedure lookup, the writer whose items are followed most closely becomes net harmful off-type, and the harm persists on top of adapters that already carry the missing competence.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Verified via s2cli (S2+HF): arXiv:2608.14036, 'Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't' (2026-08-14), which runs a contrastive study concluding that skills help mainly by acting as procedural anchors that stabilize execution rather than by injecting missing knowledge, and catalogues failure modes when the anchor does not match. That is the mechanism half of this proposal's headline already argued in print. It does not threaten the whole proposal: it holds out no task type, does not swap the writer, and has no weights arm. Two more verified papers each take a slice: arXiv:2607.28272 (MemHarness, verified) already reports that verbatim replay of retrieved experience causes negative transfer out of distribution (the proposal concedes this and correctly notes it lacks a weights arm), and arXiv:2603.18272 (Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience, verified, cit 5) already reports that retrieval-aware LoRA fine-tuning generalizes to unseen tasks - which is the positive half of P3 with a better-designed training arm than the one proposed here. Also close and NOT in the proposal's check: arXiv:2607.10608 'The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory' (verified, 2026-07-12), which finds that early adoption of conflicting retrieved memory compounds into failure and disproportionately harms stronger agents - a published version of the proposal's 'harm is a following behaviour' and of P2's harm-tracks-following coupling, on conflicting rather than wrong-type memory and without a weights arm. Unverified from memory: Yoran et al., arXiv:2310.01558 (returned by my home-literature query, abstract only), whose finding that fine-tuning on a mix of relevant and irrelevant contexts makes retrieval-augmented models robust to irrelevant context sets the prior against which P4 must be read.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline is confirmatory, and the part that is not confirmatory is under-controlled. (a) P1 is close to already known on this node: the brief reports that Measurement A's gain is carried by the clean/heat/cool procedures with unseen approximately equal to seen ('procedure-bound' in the brief's own words), that the type-agnostic six-procedure prompt is -20.1 under k=3, and that the wrong-type placebo blind1 is -3 under k=0. Removing the target type's procedure from the bank and finding the gain gone, with a small negative from wrong-type items, is the predicted continuation of measurements already in hand, and arXiv:2608.14036 and 2607.28272 have published the mechanism. A reviewer will ask what P1 tells us that a per-type decomposition of Measurement A plus blind1 did not. (b) The genuinely new claim, 'only weights carry portable competence' (P3), rests on one QLoRA r32 recipe trained on one pool - the expert pool. No LOTO adapter is trained on the self pool in the confirmatory plan (it appears only as an optional 'if time permits' all-type ablation), so the substrate contrast is confounded with writer identity, in a round whose binding rule is that writer identity is manipulated, not observed. If the LOTO adapter beats LOTO retrieval by the predicted +20, the paper cannot say whether weights are the portable substrate or whether expert text is portable only when it is not shown verbatim. (c) P4's rival is a straw man: the adapters are trained on clean expert trajectories with no retrieved context in the prompt, so nothing in training could have taught robustness to wrong-type retrieved items; the literature (2310.01558, and 2603.18272's retrieval-aware fine-tuning) says the arm that would make weights robust is one this plan does not run. 'Harm survives weights' is therefore close to guaranteed by the training recipe rather than informative about knowledge versus following. (d) The 'following behaviour, not knowledge deficit' conclusion is inferred from a success-rate difference alone; no adherence measure (rate at which the agent emits the retrieved item's appliance or step sequence) is in the per-cell metric list, so distraction and following are not separated. (e) The proposal asserts two properties its own numbers deny: P2a predicts +9 against a +6 boundary at MDE +/-5.7 (less than one MDE, contradicting the stated 'each value at least one MDE from the boundary' rule) and P3b's +12 is the algebraic sum of P3a's +6, P2c's -4 and an uncontrolled static-5 gain, contradicting 'no clause follows from the others'. Both were flagged by the automated entailment check and neither is acknowledged in the risk section.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1. Promote the self-pool LOTO adapter (matched collection and training cost) into the confirmatory set and make the substrate claim a writer x substrate 2x2 - only then can 'weights carry portable competence' be stated rather than 'the expert pool does'. 2. Add a retrieval-aware LOTO adapter, trained with wrong-type retrieved items in context (2603.18272 / 2310.01558 style), as P4's real rival; the interesting claim is that even this adapter keeps following wrong-type procedures, not that a retrieval-naive one does. 3. Add a procedure-adherence metric per episode (fraction of the retrieved item's appliance and action steps that the agent emits, and time-to-first-deviation) so the 'following' interpretation is measured, and report it against the graft control which gives its ceiling. 4. Replace the five-procedure static arm with the LOTO analog of static3 (three fixed exemplars from non-target types, token-matched), since static3 (+12.4 over k=0) is the measured best static arm on this node and the six-procedure list is the weak one (+9.5, and -20.1 under k=3); as written P3a can be won against a baseline the brief already binds proposals not to use. 5. Repair the two clauses the entailment check flags: run cells 6 and 7 at 8 seeds and move P2a's boundary to +4; restate P3b net of the static-5 prompt with its own pre-registered gain. 6. Pre-declare the writer set instead of the '>= +16 within-type gain' premise filter, which currently allows a writer with a positive LOTO gain to be dropped post hoc, and drop or explicitly power the 2-seed LOTO cells whose +/-8 MDE equals the +8 decision boundary. 7. Sharpen the framing from 'ALFWorld gains are type-bound' to the reusable methodological claim, and support it with a short audit of how many published transfer results use within-type banks - that audit, not the ALFWorld numbers, is what makes the paper matter beyond this node.
reviews.missing_baseline: A LOTO QLoRA adapter trained on the reader's own self pool at matched collection and training cost (currently only an optional all-type 'if time permits' ablation). Without it the writer variable, which the round makes binding, is manipulated only in the retrieval arm, and the P3 substrate flip cannot be attributed to the substrate. Second, and specific to P4: an adapter trained with retrieved (including wrong-type) items in context - the arm 2603.18272 and 2310.01558 say produces robustness - without which 'harm survives weights' tests a recipe rather than a hypothesis. Third: the LOTO analog of static3 (three fixed non-target-type exemplars, token-matched), rather than the five-procedure list, as the static reference for P3a.
reviews.preprint_collision: No VERIFIED COLLISION found: no preprint I retrieved runs a leave-one-type-out experience bank with writer identity manipulated and a matched weights arm. Queries run, all answered by channel (a), the s2cli command over Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers (WebSearch is unavailable in this session, so channel (b) was not used): Q1 'held-out task type evaluation of retrieved agent experience memory transfer type-bound gain' --recent -> 2608.04003 (PAST-Bench), 2607.28272 (MemHarness), 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap), 2606.02461 (AgentCL), 2604.27003 (When Continual Learning Moves to Memory), 2603.29093 (APEX-EM) - no type holdout. Q2 (all years) 'leave-one-task-out held out task category retrieval augmented agent unseen task type generalization experience bank' -> 2603.18272, 2605.20616 (Auto-Dreamer), 2501.01702 (AgentRefine) - none holds out a type from the bank. Q3 (closest named method) 'MemHarness reconstruction retrieved experience negative transfer out of distribution LLM agent' -> 2607.28272 (cit 1), 2606.04536, 2604.27003, 2608.00017 - MemHarness confirmed as the closest published statement of the harm, still without a weights arm. Q4 (home literature) 'fine-tuning makes retrieval augmented model robust to irrelevant retrieved context distraction' -> 2310.01558, 2505.06914, 2410.05983, 2505.15561 - the robustness-by-training result the proposal's P4 must be positioned against and does not cite. Q5 --recent 'ALFWorld task type holdout experience reuse same-task procedure retrieval versus LoRA parametric memory matched cost' -> 2609.02217 (SkillGLoW, 2026-09-02, procedural-family consolidation: 'the missing unit of reuse is the solving procedure shared by a cluster of related tasks'), 2606.06087 (LatentSkill: in-context textual skills converted to LoRA adapters, i.e. the substrate move of P3 already published on other grounds). Q6 --recent 'gains from retrieved trajectories vanish on unseen task categories skill library generalization held-out category negative gain' -> 2608.14036 (Demystifying Agent Skills), 2601.04992. IDs verified with s2cli paper: 2607.28272, 2603.18272, 2607.10608, 2604.27003, 2605.27762 (PEAM), 2605.26350 (When Correct Demonstrations Hurt), 2608.31100 (S3Gym), 2608.26103 (Zero-WAM), 2608.14036, 2609.02217; 2608.04003, 2606.02461, 2606.04536, 2603.29093 confirmed as search hits with matching titles. I could not verify 2310.01558's method details beyond its abstract, and I did not verify 2605.23899, 2605.30723 or 2608.07169 (brief-side, not load-bearing for this proposal's novelty argument). Judging the proposal's own check: it is above average for this round - four labelled queries with channels, a home-vocabulary query, one ID verified by hand, and an honest negative - but it is incomplete in two ways that matter. It missed 2608.14036, which publishes the 'skills are procedural anchors, not knowledge' mechanism the proposal treats as its own finding, and 2607.10608, which publishes the compliance/following account of harm from conflicting retrieved memory. It also searched only agent-side vocabulary for the weights arm and so missed the retrieval-robustness-by-fine-tuning literature (2310.01558 and relatives) that makes P4's stated rival implausible. Novelty is scored on the split design, which is genuinely unclaimed, not on the mechanism claims, which are partly claimed already.
